description: PROSE at a §40.8 default-logic body-top — including two deliberate keyword near-misses, `if you want the archive` and `Items for sale (all of them)` — does NOT fire E-CONTROL-FLOW-IN-MARKUP, and still RENDERS. A COUNTER-gate: it fails an implementation for OVER-reaching, not for under-reaching.
rationale: ⚑ THIS IS A COUNTER-GATE AND THAT IS ITS WHOLE VALUE. Prose at this position renders and is a WORKING SHAPE — S368 refused the 'diagnose every non-declaration run' limb precisely to protect it. Any future recognizer at this locus (the §40.8 arm of E-CONTROL-FLOW-IN-MARKUP is HELD at S383 pending a grammar-derived implementation — see `docs/changes/ruling3-grammar-derived/PROBLEM-STATEMENT.md`) must leave every line here alone. The two near-misses are chosen against the S203 recognizer's actual structure — it requires the keyword PLUS a `( ... )` head PLUS an opening `{`, so `if you want` fails on the missing paren head and `for sale (all of them) ship` fails on the missing `{`. MEASURED at this revision: zero errors and zero warnings, and all three prose lines appear in the emitted `<body>`. ⚠ THE FALSE-POSITIVE RISK, recorded rather than hidden: prose that genuinely spells a keyword, a parenthesis group and an opening brace — `if (you ask) { we deliver }` — WOULD match a recognizer of that shape. A corpus measurement over 2,408 sources found zero instances. ⚑ AND CORPUS-ZERO WAS NEVER SAFETY HERE. That figure was measured against a SINGLE-LINE shape only, and the recognizer's head was unbounded (`\([^]*?\)`) and crossed newlines — so at this locus, where a text run is EVERY contiguous non-markup line, the head could join a prose line to a LATER statement's brace. PA-REPRODUCED: `if (you get stuck) contact support.` followed by `function greet() { return 1 }` matched across both lines, failed the compile, and DELETED `greet` from the emitted HTML while the prior compiler emitted it clean. The multi-line axis therefore has its OWN case, `ctrl-012-default-logic-multiline-prose-neg`; a corpus that varies one axis certifies one axis. ⛑ S383 (R3) — `notCodePrefixes` MAKES THE SILENCE CLAIM ENFORCED RATHER THAN NARRATED. `codes: []` asserts NOTHING: `run.ts:441` computes `missing` by filtering the LISTED codes, so an empty list can never be violated, and `notCodes` constrains exactly one code. This case says the compiler is silent here, so it now forbids the whole `E-` and `W-` families (`run.ts:446-450`). MEASURED before pinning, through the runner rather than by hand: with `E-`, `W-` AND `I-` all forbidden, this case reports ZERO prefix violations. `I-` is deliberately left unpinned — the advisory/lint stream is a separate partition (S92/S93) and may legitimately gain hints at this locus without that being a regression here.
